title: The Blaschka Object Network — M. Otto W. Möller Hamburg Forwarding Register
actor: M. Otto W. Möller / M. O. W. Möller, Hamburg
role: Hamburg forwarding intermediary in Damon-mediated British and Irish orders
scope: Direct workshop-side evidence for Möller's handling of Blaschka marine-model consignments in 1887, with a guarded earlier Dublin/Haddon record whose OCR reads 'M.Miller' and may represent the same Hamburg forwarder. The register preserves case marks, insurance, invoice/account layers, onward consignee instructions and transport-failure feedback where legible.
name_guard: The longer form 'M. Otto W. Moller' occurs in the 11 October 1887 workshop OCR; the Liverpool record abbreviates the name to 'M. O. W. Moller'. A mid-1887 Dublin/Haddon record reads 'M.Miller' in OCR and is therefore treated only as a probable earlier occurrence pending image verification. The spelling Möller is a normalized German form for discovery only. No modern company or later Hamburg Möller business is identified as the same firm without contemporary directory evidence.

events.date: 17 June [1887?]; day/month legible in OCR, year corrupt and retained as uncertain
events.customer: Alfred Cort Haddon, Royal College of Science, Dublin
events.case_mark: OCR reads L.D. 262; original image required before normalizing the prefix
events.forwarder: OCR reads 'M.Miller' in Hamburg; probable M. Otto W. Möller but not promoted to certain identity
events.dealer_account: Workshop OCR records 695 Marks prepaid and approximately 200 Marks remaining to Damon credit.

linked_failure_feedback.customer: Prof. W. J. Sollas, Trinity College Dublin
linked_failure_feedback.event: A preceding Dublin consignment reached Sollas about two weeks late because, according to the workshop letter, a mistake in the shipper's note caused it to be landed at Bristol.
linked_failure_feedback.damage: Models numbered 239 and 356 are reported broken, probably as a consequence of the misrouting/handling sequence.
linked_failure_feedback.response: Fresh examples were enclosed with Haddon's consignment as replacements.
linked_failure_feedback.guard: The continuation OCR states that the workshop disclaimed compensation for transport damage in this context, but the addressee and exact contractual wording should be checked against the manuscript image before quotation.

events.research_value: This record ties insurance, Hamburg forwarding, invoice/accounting and a contemporaneous failure report together. It also shows repair/replacement knowledge moving across separate institutional orders: Sollas's damaged models were replaced inside Haddon's outgoing case.

events.date: 1887-10-11 letter; case dispatched 1887-10-08 according to workshop text
events.onward_recipient: Rev. T. A. Preston, Marlborough-area address as OCR-read; exact address requires image verification
events.dealer_account: Workshop letter records 443 Marks prepaid and approximately 242 Marks remaining to Damon's credit after the invoice; arithmetic/OCR should be checked against the manuscript image before publication.
events.research_value: The source explicitly connects case mark, model destination, insured value, forwarding firm, onward consignee, invoice and dealer credit in one transaction document.

events.date: early December 1887; exact day to be image-verified
events.onward_recipient: Higgins, Liverpool; exact title/name should be checked against the manuscript image and Liverpool receiving-side records
events.insurance: Insurance figure is OCR-ambiguous in the dispatch record and is not normalized here.
events.invoice: 268 Marks total stated in the dispatch letter
events.preceding_value_layers: A 23 November letter states that 247 Marks already prepaid for Liverpool covered the models only and asks for about 50 Marks more for packing. These figures are preserved as distinct model-value, packing-estimate and later invoice/account layers rather than forced into one total.
events.payment_layer: The dispatch letter acknowledges a £25 draft, OCR-converted by a Dresden bank to 506 Reichsmarks, and carries remaining Damon credit forward toward Galway and Cardiff orders.
events.research_value: The source shows Möller reused as a forwarding node only weeks after Marlborough and connects the Hamburg handoff to Liverpool's case mark, invoice and rolling Damon account.

network_observation: The Hamburg forwarding route is now broader than a Liverpool microhistory. Exact Möller wording is secure for Marlborough and Liverpool; the earlier Haddon record probably points to the same firm but remains image-dependent. Across the cluster, the workshop records case identity, insurance, invoice, dealer credit and onward routing, while a Dublin misrouting to Bristol demonstrates how documentary error in the shipper's note could become delay, breakage and replacement. Missing case numbers such as I.B. 267 are not reconstructed from sequence alone.
